parts.text:
7
A stone is projected vertically upwards from the ground at an initial speed of 15 m s–1. Air
resistance is negligible.
What is the maximum height reached by the stone?
A
0.76 m
B
11 m
C
23 m
D
110 m

hints: Notice the stone starts at $15 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ upwards and its velocity is $0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ instantaneously at maximum height.
Connect this motion to $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$, with downward acceleration $a = -9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ opposing the upward displacement.
Rearrange to $h = u^2/(2g)$ and substitute $u = 15 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to compare the numerical height with the $0.76 \text{ m}$, $11 \text{ m}$, $23 \text{ m}$ and $110 \text{ m}$ options.
walkthrough: Take upwards as positive. Initial velocity $u = 15 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, final velocity at top $v = 0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, and acceleration $a = -g = -9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ because weight acts downwards.
Use the SUVAT equation without time: $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$, where $s = h$ is the maximum vertical displacement.
Set $v = 0$ for maximum height: $0 = u^2 - 2gh$, so $2gh = u^2$.
Substitute values with units: $h = (15 \text{ m s}^{-1})^2/(2 \times 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}) = 225/19.62 \text{ m}$.
Calculate the intermediate result $h \approx 11.5 \text{ m}$, which to the precision of the options is about $11 \text{ m}$ with correct unit $\text{m}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: Too small for $15 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ launch speed. It does not follow from $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $v=0$ and $a=-g$.

B.explanation: Follows from $0 = u^2 - 2gh$, giving $h = u^2/(2g) \approx 11 \text{ m}$ for $u = 15 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

C.explanation: About twice the correct height. It results from omitting the factor 2 and using $h = u^2/g$.

D.explanation: Far too large, close to $u^2/2$. It results from omitting $g$ and not using $h = u^2/(2g)$.
